tob-10825: G. R. S. Mead assembled this selection from five years of Theosophical journals, gathering key essays on karma, reincarnation, and the hidden masters said to guide humanity. Contributors include Blavatsky and the movement’s leading thinkers. The volume offers a compact survey of what Theosophy taught at the height of its influence.
tob-13325: Claud Field’s translation of al-Ghazali’s spiritual autobiography follows the great Muslim thinker through his crisis of faith. Weary of empty argument, he abandons his professorship to seek God through Sufi contemplation. His account of doubt, despair, and final peace has made this one of the most human documents of medieval Islam.
tob-4025: Descartes’s Meditations lead the reader through six days of root-and-branch doubt — from cheating senses to the proof of God and the clean split of mind and body. William Molyneux’s early English version bore this founding text of modern thought to British readers. It stays the classic drill in thinking from zero.
tob-4125: Herbert Giles’s Chuang Tzu shows the Taoist sage as holy man, moral teacher, and gadfly in one. His free, merry rendering lets Zhuangzi’s butterflies, good-for-nothing trees, and laughing sages charm at full strength. Giles’s framing pieces set the thinker against the Confucian order he teased.
tob-4225: The Arbatel of Wonder — Latin 1575, Turner’s English 1655 — is the gentlest of wonder-books, teaching the Olympian ghosts’ art through prayer and cleanness. Its nine books promise wisdom to the worthy. The work fed later Rosy-Cross thinking. A wonder-book of unwonted mildness.
tob-13725: The third of Mead’s Thrice-Greatest Hermes books crowns his great Hermes-study — its strewn bits, out-takings, and olden witnesses. His Englishing and gloss made Thrice-Great Hermes open to our readers. The books stay the classic English handling of the Hermetica.
cia-0000109825: An October 1945 document: a statement prepared to clear the name of someone called Schmalfuss — the archive's punctuation garbles the details. In postwar Germany, reputations meant survival, and statements of innocence were currency. The entry is a small, human fragment of the denazification era's paperwork.
cia-0000112825: An interrogation report on Fritz Emme, estimated to date from October 1945. Questioning detainees was how the Allies unraveled the enemy's networks — one interview at a time. The entry preserves the form if not the content: the fact of the interrogation, filed and kept.
cia-0000115525: A July 1967 clandestine service history of the Berlin Tunnel operation of 1952 to 1956 — the CIA's audacious tap of Soviet military phone lines under East Berlin. Dug in secret and betrayed by a mole, the tunnel still yielded a flood of intelligence. The history is spycraft legend, told by the agency itself.
cia-0000119725: A September 1956 report, its title garbled, on a silent demonstration during the reburial of Laszlo Rajk — the communist leader executed in a show trial, now rehabilitated. Tens of thousands marched in quiet protest at his funeral. The document captures grief turning into politics — the revolution's dress rehearsal.
cia-0000132225: Situation Report 542, its paragraph header deleted, on Iraqi planes — the truncated title withholds the story. Saddam's air force was being destroyed on the ground and in the air. The redacted entry keeps its number in the long march of daily reports.
cia-0000132425: A January 1960 report on Venezuelan-Cuban relations. Democratic Venezuela and revolutionary Cuba were on a collision course — Caracas would soon break with Havana. The document watches the rift forming: two revolutions, diverging.
cia-0000132625: A June 1960 report: communists continuing to expand their role in the Castro regime. The party was tightening its grip on the revolution. The document is the expansion: the communists, advancing.
cia-0000135825: A 1954 basic document, number one — its subject deleted. The foundation paper of some operation, its topic censored. The entry is the cornerstone: the plan's basis, withheld.
cia-0000135925: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting guidance on recent arrests. The other side was rounding people up — the operation needed direction. The document is the alarm: the arrests, reported — the guidance, requested.
cia-0000136125: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the QQ program — the archive's punctuation doubles the quote. The cryptonym, invoked. The entry is the program: the QQ, referenced.
cia-0000136225: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN, from WELLBANK, for discussion with PAGE on SWALLOW. The cryptonym, discussed. The entry is the talk: the subject, coded.
cia-0000137325: The NSC briefing of April 28, 1960, with an attached document titled NSC Briefing minus the rest — the truncated title cuts off the subject. The spring briefing. The document is the session: April's, briefed.
un-ga-res-a-69-25: Resolution A/69/25, cataloged with the year 1981 — again the mismatch. The entry records the designation and flags the inconsistency, inventing nothing.
un-ga-res-25: UN General Assembly Resolution 25, adopted in 1946. The twenty-fifth act of the first Assembly. The number and year endure; the decision waits in the text.
un-ga-res-2625: General Assembly Resolution 2625, adopted in October 1970 — the Friendly Relations Declaration, the landmark statement of the basic principles of international law: sovereign equality, no force, self-determination. On the UN's 25th anniversary, the Assembly codified the rules of coexistence. The resolution is the charter's companion: the principles, declared.
un-ga-res-44-25: General Assembly Resolution 44/25, adopted in November 1989 — the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history. It gave children around the world legal rights to survival, protection, and participation. The resolution is the promise: the children, protected.
un-sc-res-125: Security Council Resolution 125, adopted in 1957. The late-fifties Council at work. The designation and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-425: Security Council Resolution 425, adopted in March 1978 — the Lebanon resolution, calling for Israel's withdrawal from southern Lebanon and creating the UN Interim Force in Lebanon. Born of invasion, UNIFIL has kept its watch for nearly five decades. The resolution is the force: the peacekeepers, deployed.
un-sc-res-825: Security Council Resolution 825, adopted in May 1993 — the North Korea resolution, calling on Pyongyang to reconsider its withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. The Council's first answer to the nuclear crisis. The resolution is the plea: the treaty, honored.
un-sc-res-1025: Security Council Resolution 1025, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The mid-nineties Council at work. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1325: Security Council Resolution 1325, cataloged with the year 1998 — though the landmark women, peace and security resolution belongs to October 2000, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-1425: Security Council Resolution 1425, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The Council's business rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1825: Security Council Resolution 1825, adopted in 2008 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
cia-0000135725: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135725, the archive's date uncertain. The approximately dated set. The entry is the approximation: the year, circa.
cia-0000136625: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136625, the archive's date uncertain. The roughly dated set. The entry is the roughness: the date, estimated.
cia-0000136725: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136725. The fateful year's documents. The entry is the fate: the year, 1961.
plos-pone-0000025: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper: the release of nitric oxide from S-nitrosothiols promotes angiogenesis — new blood-vessel growth. A gas better known as a pollutant turns out to build vessels. The paper is the promotion: the gas, constructive.
cia-0000137525: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000137525, the archive's date uncertain. The circa-dated set. The document is the circa: the dating, estimated.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d25: President Roosevelt and Prime Minister Churchill to Marshal Stalin — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 25. The two Western leaders wrote Moscow jointly. The message is the jointness: the two, as one.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d125: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the president's special assistant — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 125. Another backchannel cable. The message is the continuation: the channel, open.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d225: The Joint Chiefs of Staff to the President, November 17, 1943 — Document 225. The war's planners wrote the White House. The memo is the planners': the chiefs, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d325: A memorandum by the British Chiefs of Staff, November 26, 1943 — Document 325. Another British planners' paper. The memo is the paper: the chiefs, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d425: A log of the trip, December 2, 1943 — Document 425. The presidential journey, logged. The log is the journey: the trip, recorded.
adventures-of-huckleberry-finn-chapters-: The Duke and the King, those peerless frauds, take over the raft in these chapters, and Twain's satire bites deep. The circus, the camp meeting, and the Wilks swindle show human gullibility at full flood. Comedy with a moral sting.
arxiv-2605-08925: Segmenting a 3D scene usually means labeling thousands of points by hand. Xueyang Kang, Zijian Yu, Kourosh Khoshelham, and colleagues propose ClickSeg3D: a few clicks from the user, guided by semantic embeddings, suffice to segment the scene. The 2026 paper makes 3D annotation dramatically cheaper.
arxiv-2605-09525: Testing many hypotheses at once risks a flood of false discoveries; controlling the false discovery rate simultaneously across location families is the goal. Zijun Gao, Wenjie Hu, and Qingyuan Zhao solve it with new methodology. The 2026 paper is multiple-testing theory with simultaneous guarantees.
arxiv-2605-09725: Distilling a big teacher model into a small student works best on-policy — but which teacher rollouts deserve distilling? Ke Zhang, Yunjie Tian, Dongdi Zhao, and colleagues select the best-of-N teacher rollouts. The 2026 paper distills only the teacher's finest moments.
arxiv-2605-09825: Four-bit floating point — MXFP4 — on native FP4 hardware could slash the cost of training. Musa Cim, Poovaiah Palangappa, Miro Hodak, and colleagues pretrain large language models exactly that way. The 2026 paper is hardware-aware training at extreme low precision.
arxiv-2605-10125: AI tools in academic research — useful for exploration, risky for precision. Anthea Dathe, Kiran Hoffmann, and Aline Mangold evaluate the tradeoff. The 2026 paper is meta-science on the AI assistant. It grades the machine honestly as a research partner.
plos-pone-0003425: Geneticists tested a longevity legend in this 2008 study of Ashkenazi Jewish centenarians. Mitochondrial haplogroup J had been linked to long life in Italian and Finnish groups, so the team checked whether the longest-lived Ashkenazi Jews carried it more often. They did not, showing the supposed longevity marker does not travel with every population.
plos-pone-0003525: Theorists showed immune diversity is HIV's ceiling in this 2008 paper. Human MHC class I molecules vary wildly between people, and the team demonstrated that this very polymorphism stops HIV-1 from adapting globally to evade immune detection. What works as an escape in one person fails in the next, keeping the virus from ever winning everywhere at once.
plos-pone-0003625: Psychiatric geneticists Mudge, Miller, and Khrebtukova sequenced toward schizophrenia's roots in this 2008 study. Their genomic convergence analysis, combining mRNA sequencing with genetics, flagged altered synaptic vesicle transport in the illness. The vesicle defect points to how brain cells package and release their chemical messages going awry.
plos-pone-0003725: In 2008, Gowen, Smee, and Wong tested a late-stage rescue for hemorrhagic fever. The drug T-705 was tried against arenaviral hemorrhagic fever in an animal model, even after disease had set in. The efficacy and safety data support a treatment option for a family of viruses with few answers.
plos-pone-0003825: In 2008, Abramson, Kedem, and Relman showed whooping cough's stealth tool at work. Filamentous hemagglutinin from Bordetella pertussis tuned the NF-kB immune pathway. The modulation reveals how the bacterium tamps down host defenses while it settles in.
plos-pone-0003925: In 2008, Masashi Tachikawa showed noise splitting species on a computer. His mathematical ecosystem model found environmental fluctuation driving evolutionary branching. The systems that emerged were robust against the very noise that split them. The work suggests life's diversity feeds on the world's unsteadiness.
plos-pone-0004025: In 2008, Al Mahmud, Amore, and Bernardi found DNA neighborhoods shaping gene activity. In sea urchin embryos, the compositional genome context around genes affected expression control. The finding challenges the old view that only nearby regulatory switches matter. The broader genomic neighborhood gets a real vote in embryonic development too.
plos-pone-0004125: In 2009, Driscoll, Yamaguchi, and Bar-Gal solved a tiger mystery with DNA. Mitochondrial DNA showed the extinct Caspian tiger was close kin to the living Amur tiger. The Caspian tiger vanished from the wild around 1970. The neat finding rewrites tiger family history.
plos-pone-0004225: In 2009, Maas and Gommans found hidden code in a gene editor. A new exon of mammalian ADAR2 extended the open reading frame itself. The extra exon lengthened the RNA-editing enzyme a lot. The neat find expands the editor's known forms.
plos-pone-0004325: In 2009, Touma, Fenzl, and Ruschel bred mice for stress extremes. Mice selected for high and low stress reactivity showed shifted rhythmicity. Behavior, hormones, and sleep all changed. The lines model mood-disorder biology. The work links stress genes to body-clock disruption.
plos-pone-0358225: Fatty liver disease can harden into fibrosis and spawn liver cancer. This mouse study tested semaglutide — the well-known weight-loss drug — combined with CRV431 on liver fibrosis and liver cancer in a MASLD model. The divergent effects of the co-therapy reveal where the combination helps and where it doesn’t.
plos-pone-0358325: Patients ask chatbots about breast cancer — but which bot answers better? This comparative evaluation pitted ChatGPT against Gemini on patient-oriented breast cancer questions. The head-to-head scores tell patients and doctors which AI gives safer, more accurate answers when it matters most.
plos-pone-0354425: People with HIV in the UK don’t all use healthcare equally. This study mapped sociodemographic variations in healthcare service use among this population. The patterns reveal who is underserved — by age, background, or circumstance — and where the health system must reach further.
plos-pone-0358125: When blood returns to starved muscle, the reperfusion itself causes injury. This mouse study showed esketamine protects against skeletal muscle injury from hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion by regulating autophagy — the cell’s cleanup process. The finding hints that a drug already used in clinics could shield surgical patients’ muscles.
plos-pone-0341525: Fish farms need reliable eyes underwater, where visibility is poor and pens are crowded. YOLO-CBNet is a robust attention-enhanced detection framework for underwater fish recognition in aquaculture environments. The model keeps working in murky water and dense schools where ordinary vision AI gives up.
plos-pone-0357125: Long COVID doesn’t just sicken — it derails livelihoods. This nationwide Malaysian study measured the prevalence and risk factors of adverse work outcomes among manufacturing workers with Long COVID. The findings quantify the pandemic’s long tail on labor: lost jobs, lost income, lost capacity.
plos-pone-0357725: Do younger generations handle social isolation differently from their elders? This analysis of the European Social Survey (Round 11, 2023/2024) examined social isolation and health risks across age groups. The findings reveal whether youth are more resilient to isolation — or quietly more vulnerable.
plos-pone-0356725: Hepatitis D cannot survive without hepatitis B — a deadly viral partnership. This mathematical model of HBV–HDV transmission with superinfection examined the roles of vaccination and liver transplantation in disease dynamics. The equations guide smarter control strategies for both viruses together.
plos-pone-0357025: Right heart failure after LVAD implantation can be deadly — and predicting it saves lives. This paper validated predictive risk models for right heart failure following primary durable ventricular assist device implantation. The validated models help surgeons decide who can safely receive the life-saving device.
plos-pone-0339225: Drone swarms must navigate even when their radios fail. This paper proposed a hierarchical navigation decision-making method for UAV swarms in unknown, communication-constrained environments. The hierarchy keeps the swarm coherent and mission-capable when communication drops out — exactly when it matters most.
plos-pone-0355625: Synaptopodin is a key architect of dendritic spines — the brain’s receiving stations. This synaptopodin knockout rat gives neuroscientists a new tool for studying the dendritic spine apparatus and axonal cisternal organelles in synaptic plasticity, development, and behavior. The rat opens fresh experimental ground.
plos-pone-0356825: Cognitive behavioural therapy’s benefits for adult ADHD may endure long after sessions end. This paper studied the long-term effects of CBT on quality of life in adults with ADHD. The findings show lasting benefit — evidence that therapy’s gains aren’t just a honeymoon effect.
plos-pone-0355725: The COVID-19 Omicron wave reshaped hospital microbial ecology. This paper tracked changes in multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae among emergency room patients during the pandemic. The shifting resistance patterns warn that viral pandemics leave bacterial consequences in their wake.
plos-pone-0352025: European children born with congenital anomalies die at rates that track their families’ socioeconomic status. This EUROLINKCAT cohort study examined those associations across the continent. The findings expose a brutal inequity: birth defects are democratic in occurrence but aristocratic in survival — demanding health systems that protect every child equally.
plos-pone-0354125: Neck posture might affect how we recover from stumbles. This paper studied how cervical spine posture influences susceptibility to walking balance perturbations. The findings connect the neck’s position to whole-body stability — with implications for fall prevention and rehabilitation.
europmc-pmc2793425: Could a blood test warn of ovarian cancer before symptoms appear? This 2009 paper reports a pattern of chemical marks on DNA in blood samples that signals active ovarian cancer. The epigenetic signature, meaning changes in gene activity rather than gene sequence, predicted disease in the study. If confirmed, such a test could catch a cancer that is usually found too late.
europmc-pmc2811725: Women are born with all the eggs they will ever have, and this 2010 paper models how that stock declines. The authors build a mathematical picture of the human ovarian reserve from conception through menopause. Their curve predicts fertility loss with age. The model gave doctors a quantitative tool for counseling women about reproductive lifespan.
europmc-pmc2818025: Aging cells release inflammatory signals that harm their neighbors, and this 2009 paper finds tiny RNAs that dial them down. The authors show microRNAs miR-146a and miR-146b reduce the inflammatory mediators IL-6 and IL-8 in senescent cells. The discovery reveals a built-in brake on age-related inflammation. It pointed to new ways of easing the damage aging cells cause.
europmc-pmc2824625: Athletes have long relied on caffeine, and this 2010 position stand gives the science behind the habit. The International Society of Sports Nutrition reviews the evidence on caffeine and performance, concluding it genuinely aids endurance and focus. The authors also cover dosing and timing. The statement became the reference for evidence-based caffeine use in sport.
europmc-pmc2837025: Predicting which breast cancers will return is a high-stakes task. This 2010 paper develops methods to detect gene pathways with predictive power for breast cancer prognosis. The authors show pathway-level signals beat single genes. Their approach moved prognosis from gene lists toward biology that makes sense.
europmc-pmc2910725: Stem cells mail tiny packages stuffed with gene-tweaking RNAs. This 2010 paper shows small bubbles from marrow and tissue stem cells ferry chosen microRNAs. The authors reveal a working delivery post between cells. Their find matters for healing medicine, hinting that cell-free therapies could one day replace cell transplants.
europmc-pmc2919425: Fighting malaria in Africa needs smart plans. This 2010 paper runs math models to weigh ways of cutting the main malaria germ's spread. The authors pit bed nets, drugs, and sprays head to head. Their models guide real-world crusades. The results help funders pick the mix that saves the most lives per dollar.
europmc-pmc2924325: RNA folds into shapes, and disease mutations can warp them. This 2010 paper studies disease-linked mutations that alter the RNA structural ensemble. The authors show one sequence can fold many ways, and one warp breaks it. Their work links RNA misfolding to human illness.
europmc-pmc2955025: PCR results need standards to be trusted. This 2010 paper gives a practical guide for implementing MIQE minimum guidelines for quantitative real-time PCR. The authors' checklist curbs sloppy reporting. Their work lifted a workhorse method. Journals now demand MIQE details with submissions.
europmc-pmc2958125: Breast cells release microRNAs selectively, and cancer changes the mix. This 2010 paper compares microRNA release from normal and malignant mammary cells. The authors find selective export shifts in cancer. Their work hints at blood tests. A blood draw might one day spot tumors early.
europmc-pmc2993925: Twitter chatter tracked the 2009 swine flu. This 2010 paper studies tweets sent during the H1N1 outbreak. The authors show social media mirrors epidemics in real time. Their work launched digital disease tracking. Health agencies now mine feeds for early warnings.
europmc-pmc2996325: Prion detection got fast and sensitive. This 2010 paper brings a quick test that spots prion seeding as well as slow animal tests. The authors' assay speeds diagnosis hugely. Their work aids mad cow surveillance. Blood banks may one day screen donors.
europmc-pmc2998425: Stem cells calm sore joints through a chemical messenger. This 2010 paper shows marrow stem cells release a soothing signal that eases arthritis in mice. The authors trace the calming chain. Their work backs stem cell therapy. Joint injections may one day replace pills.
europmc-pmc3024225: Mild brain zaps can tune working memory. This 2011 study shows gentle current to the forehead shifts working memory scores. The authors back it with behavior and brain-wave data. Their work opened the cognitive-enhancement debate. Effects fade within hours, they note.
europmc-pmc3053525: Sticky drug delivery got a review. This 2011 review covers medicines that cling to moist body linings. The authors survey the sticky tech. Their overview guides drug formulators. Patches cling inside cheeks for hours. The tech dodges stomach acid damage. Vaccines may ride the sticky route next.
europmc-pmc3065425: Celiac and gluten sensitivity differ in the gut. This 2011 paper compares leaky-gut and immune signals in the two gluten conditions. The authors reveal the split. Their work clarifies the diagnoses. Only celiac showed true barrier breakdown. Doctors now test before prescribing diets.
europmc-pmc6507025: Baicalin is a plant compound drawn from the root of Chinese skullcap, long used in traditional medicine. Scientists tested it in mice with inflammation-driven depression-like symptoms and found it eased them. The effect runs through a specific chain of cell signals that quiets an immune sensor called TLR4, calming brain inflammation and the low mood that follows it.
europmc-pmc6605025: Some bacteria are natural clumpers: cells of the same kind stick together into aggregates that sink out of liquid. This review explores autoaggregation - why bacteria glom onto their own kind, from surface proteins to environmental cues. The clumping shapes biofilms, infections, and even how we might trap germs.
europmc-pmc6608625: Fitting atomic models into blurry cryo-EM maps is part art, part grind. Namdinator automates the fitting with molecular dynamics: it gently flexes the model until it settles into the experimental map. Structural biologists get faster, more reliable models from low-resolution data.
europmc-pmc6610925: Cancers sweeten their proteins with sugar tags - and the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway cooks up the raw material. This review shows how the HBP funnels glucose and other fuels into the building blocks for glycosylation, feeding tumor growth. Choking this metabolic side street could slow cancers that lean on it.
europmc-pmc6657025: War shatters minds as well as bodies - but how many suffer mentally in conflict zones? This systematic review updates WHO estimates of mental disorder prevalence where fighting rages, using modern methods on a decade of data. The new numbers: roughly one in five affected, far above peacetime rates.
europmc-pmc6683325: Probiotic yogurts and drinks only work if the live bacteria survive the factory, the shelf, and the stomach. This review surveys food-system strategies for keeping probiotics viable: protective coatings, hardy strains, smarter delivery. The goal is simple - living microbes that actually reach the gut.
europmc-pmc6773825: Immune systems age too - growing slower, weaker, and more inflammatory. This review catalogs the hallmarks of immunosenescence and asks how to oppose aging strategically: vaccines, lifestyle, and emerging therapies. The playbook for keeping old immune systems young.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-25: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report finding that trends in energy derivatives markets were raising questions about the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's oversight. New trading venues and products were growing faster than the regulator's grasp. GAO's analysis landed as energy prices surged — and as lawmakers began asking whether speculation, not supply, was driving what Americans paid.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-425: Homeland Security's tech-hiring blueprint mostly matched the guidance in 2007, GAO found — but the doing lagged the drawing. The report says the department's plan for landing and keeping computer talent needed teeth and timelines. Paper plans do not staff a cyber watch; GAO wanted the follow-through.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-825: Chemical safety, two rulebooks: GAO's 2007 report stacks America's approach against Europe's tough new law. The comparison shows where U.S. rules lagged on guarding against toxic risks. The findings landed as Congress weighed whether to toughen the home team's chemical game.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-925: Asian American and Pacific Islander students were hitting hidden walls in 2007 — GAO's report says colleges could crack them by sharing notes. The findings argue the ‘model minority' myth masked real struggles. The report's fix is humble: talk to each other, and the patterns emerge.
openalex-w7204840425: Are we free because we choose, or do we choose because we understand? This philosophy paper studies the roles of will and intellect in human freedom through the Aristotelian, Augustinian, and Thomist traditions. The author traces how these thinkers linked knowing and wanting. Dense but rewarding, it tackles one of philosophy's oldest questions with the tools of the classical tradition.
pmc-13499225: This 2026 paper reviews efforts toward precision medicine in juvenile idiopathic arthritis — tailoring treatment to each child's biology rather than using one-size-fits-all drugs. The authors survey biomarkers, genetics, and trial designs moving the field forward. For kids with chronic joint disease, getting the right drug first matters enormously.
pmc-13439725: This 2026 study compared sexual health behaviors and contraceptive practices among Canadian childhood, adolescent, and young adult cancer survivors versus controls. Cancer treatment can affect fertility and intimacy, and the comparison reveals where survivors need more support. The findings guide follow-up care for young survivors.
pmc-13437925: This 2026 immunology paper maps the TG2/LRP1 pathway by which T cells get activated by post-translationally modified antigens — proteins altered after they're built, as happens in celiac disease and rheumatoid arthritis. Understanding the activation route could reveal ways to calm misguided immunity.
pmc-13428725: A 2026 correction notice for a paper on the immunological impact of tumor-draining lymph node dissection on systemic Th1-like CD4+ T cells in early-stage lung cancer. Formal corrections keep the scientific record accurate when published details need amending. This entry preserves the correction as issued.
pmc-13428025: In this 2026 pharmacovigilance study, researchers mined FDA and Canadian safety databases for reported anaphylaxis linked to glatiramer acetate, a multiple sclerosis drug. Severe allergic reactions are rare but critical to document. The analysis characterizes how often and in what form they occur.
pmc-13595325: In this 2026 study, researchers linked maternal adiposity during pregnancy to differences in newborns' brain cortical development. The association between a mother's body composition and the baby's cortex adds to evidence that pregnancy shapes brain architecture. The work underscores the importance of maternal metabolic health.
pmc-13413625: A 2026 scoping review of environmental performance indicators used in healthcare foodservices — how hospitals measure the green footprint of feeding patients. Food is a major slice of hospital emissions, and the review catalogs what gets measured. It gives sustainability teams a starting framework.
pmc-13523825: This 2026 paper examined the durability of gene therapy for sickle cell disease — how long the one-time treatment's benefits last. Durability is the make-or-break question for curative gene therapies. The analysis addresses what patients and payers most need to know.
pmc-13440125: A 2026 multi-institutional Japanese retrospective study of real-world outcomes of definitive chemoradiotherapy for bladder cancer. Bladder preservation without surgery is the goal. The real-world data complement trial evidence.
pmc-13539925: This 2026 paper proposed an integrated immuno-tubular model of tubular dysfunction in Sjögren's disease-associated renal tubular acidosis. The autoimmune disease attacks moisture glands — and sometimes kidneys. The model connects immune mechanisms to the kidney's acid-handling failure.
pmc-13424525: A 2026 bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study of causal relationships between aging-related biomarkers and osteoporosis. Genetics sorted cause from correlation. The causal arrows are the finding.
pmc-13525525: In this 2026 case study and literature review, Ureaplasma parvum meningitis in neonates was examined. The unusual pathogen's brain infection was characterized. The review is the reference.
pmc-13510125: In this 2026 nanotechnology paper, copper nanoparticles were green-synthesized using Grevillea robusta (silky oak) extract — with in vitro antimicrobial testing and in silico analysis. The plant-made particles killed microbes. The green synthesis is the appeal.
pmc-13472325: This 2026 paper demonstrated autonomous molecular sensing with a chemically stateful solid-state nanopore. The smart pore sensed molecules. The statefulness is the innovation.
pmc-13445625: This 2026 mouse study tested human placental tissue-derived xenograft impact on bone healing and pain behaviors in a segmental bone defect model. The placental graft aided healing. The impact is the finding.
pmc-13443325: A 2026 dermatopathology paper on diagnostic usefulness of immunohistochemical staining for EMA in psoriasis and atopic dermatitis showing psoriasiform hyperplasia. The stain's diagnostic value was tested. The usefulness is the finding.
pmc-13427625: This 2026 paper chemically optimized temporin A-L peptides — from native isoforms to enhanced antimicrobial analogs. The frog peptides were improved. The optimization is the drug design.
pmc-13472725: In this 2026 paper, MoESurv — a zero-sample and transferable survival prediction framework for rare cancers using mixture of experts — was introduced. The AI predicted without training data. The transferability is the breakthrough.
pmc-13439925: This 2026 paper showed progressive suppression of DNA repair genes with persistent p53 target activation in doxorubicin-treated cardiomyocytes. The chemo's heart damage mechanism was detailed. The suppression is the cardiotoxicity pathway.
pmc-13526525: This 2026 paper showed stem cell factor regulated endothelial HIF-2alpha expression during hypoxia-driven pathological angiogenesis. The growth factor's vascular role was defined. The regulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13468125: In this 2026 paper, nitrogen-fixing trees shifted soil organic carbon toward mineral-associated stability by enhancing microbial-derived carbon in subtropical plantations. The trees stabilized the soil carbon. The shifting is the climate insight.
pmc-13615225: A 2026 paper harnessing brain age-specific effects on associations between sleep quality, glymphatic function, and cognition in normal ageing adults (the title is truncated). The sleep-brain-cognition triangle was age-stratified. The harnessing is the analytical advance.
pmc-13461825: A 2026 immuno-oncology review: "Beyond KIR and NKG2A blockade" — reprogramming NK-cell immunity in solid tumors. The natural killer cell strategies were surveyed. The reprogramming is the therapeutic frontier.
pmc-13417725: This 2026 Nepalese coprological investigation examined endoparasites in one-horned rhinoceros outside Chitwan National Park. The rhinos' parasites were cataloged. The investigation serves conservation.
pmc-13616125: A 2026 scoping review of reviews on acceptability of oral health care — to inform framework development. The dental care acceptance literature was synthesized. The review is the implementation input.
arxiv-2606-16125: Black holes ring like bells when disturbed, emitting gravitational waves at characteristic frequencies called quasinormal modes. This paper studies those ringing patterns — and the associated Hawking radiation — for black holes with "primary scalar hair," extra fields that violate the classic no-hair theorem. It targets researchers in gravitational physics.
arxiv-2606-16425: Shallow quantum circuits — few layers of operations — are the realistic kind for near-term hardware. This paper establishes a worst-case depth hierarchy: some problems genuinely need deeper shallow circuits than others, no cleverness can dodge it. It targets quantum complexity theorists mapping what near-term quantum computers can do.
arxiv-2606-16825: Mixture-of-experts models split the work among 'expert' sub-networks. This paper ties those expert layers together — sharing weights between experts ('tying the loop') — to cut size without losing skill. It is for researchers compressing big MoE language models. Shared weights, slimmer giants.
